rows.stem: What are minisatellites ?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 – 40 bp sized small sequences within the genes.

options.label: B
options.text: Short coding repetitive sequences region on the eukaryotic genome.

options.label: C
options.text: Short non-coding repetitive sequences forming a large portion of eukaryotic genome.

options.label: D
options.text: Regions of coding strand of DNA.

rows.solution: A large portion of the human genome is made of **repetitive DNA**: small stretches of DNA repeated many times. Depending on base composition, length of segment and number of repetitive units, this satellite DNA is classified into categories such as **micro-satellites and mini-satellites**. These sequences normally **do not code for any proteins**, but they **form a large portion of the human genome**, and they show a high degree of polymorphism, which is why they are the basis of DNA fingerprinting. They are not coding sequences and they do not lie within genes. So the answer is option (C) Short non-coding repetitive sequences forming a large portion of eukaryotic genome.

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.stem: Identify the incorrect statement regarding PCR.

options.label: A
options.text: Two sets of primers are required during polymerisation.

options.label: B
options.text: The process of replication is repeated multiple times to produce one billion copies.

options.label: C
options.text: Thermostable DNA polymerase is used for extension of primers.

options.label: D
options.text: Annealing is required to separate both the strands of template DNA.

rows.solution:
Each PCR cycle has three steps:
- **Denaturation**: the double-stranded template DNA is heated so that its **two strands separate**.
- **Annealing**: two sets of primers bind (anneal) to the single strands.
- **Extension**: a thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) extends the primers.

The cycle is repeated many times, amplifying the segment to about one billion copies. Strand separation is done by denaturation, not by annealing, so that statement is the incorrect one. So the answer is option (D) Annealing is required to separate both the strands of template DNA.

rows.stem: The following information is about drugs and tobacco. Select the correct statement from the options given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Cocaine is given to patients after surgery as it stimulates recovery.

options.label: B
options.text: Chewing tobacco lowers blood pressure and heart rate.

options.label: C
options.text: Barbiturates when given to criminals makes them tell the truth.

options.label: D
options.text: Morphine is often given to persons who have undergone surgery as a painkiller.

rows.solution:
- Cocaine is a stimulant of the central nervous system that interferes with the transport of dopamine; it is a drug of abuse, not a post-operative treatment.
- Tobacco contains nicotine, which stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline and nor-adrenaline, so it **raises** blood pressure and heart rate.
- Barbiturates are sedatives; they are not used to make criminals tell the truth.
- **Morphine**, extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, is a very effective **sedative and painkiller** and is very useful in patients who have undergone surgery.

So the answer is option (D) Morphine is often given to persons who have undergone surgery as a painkiller.

Which of the following conditions correctly describes the manner of determining the sex in the given options ?

options.label: A
options.text: Homozygous sex chromosomes (ZZ) determine female sex in birds.

options.label: B
options.text: XO type of chromosomes determine male sex in grasshoppers.

options.label: C
options.text: XO condition in humans determines female sex.

options.label: D
options.text: Homozygous sex chromosomes (XX) produce male in Drosophila.

rows.solution:
- In birds, the **female is heterogametic (ZW)** and the male is homogametic (ZZ), so ZZ determines the male sex, not the female.
- In grasshoppers, males have only one X chromosome besides the autosomes (**XO type**), while females have a pair of X chromosomes. So XO does determine the **male** sex in grasshoppers.
- In humans, sex is determined by the XX (female) and XY (male) mechanism; an XO individual is a case of Turner's syndrome, a chromosomal disorder, not the manner of determining sex.
- In Drosophila, XX produces the **female** and XY the male.

So the answer is option (B) XO type of chromosomes determine male sex in grasshoppers.

rows.stem: Choose the option that correctly describes the gynoecium of Michelia :

options.label: A
options.text: Multicarpellary, Apocarpous

options.label: B
options.text: Bicarpellary, Apocarpous

options.label: C
options.text: Multicarpellary, Syncarpous

options.label: D
options.text: Bicarpellary, Syncarpous

rows.solution: The gynoecium of Michelia has **many free pistils**: it is **multicarpellary** (more than one carpel) and **apocarpous** (the carpels are free), as shown in the NCERT figure of a multicarpellary, apocarpous gynoecium of Michelia. (Papaver, by contrast, has a multicarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium, with the pistils fused together.) So the answer is option (A) Multicarpellary, Apocarpous.

rows.stem:
The given graph shows the range of variation among population members, for a trait determined by multiple genes. If this population is subjected to disruptive selection for several generations, which of the following distributions is most likely to result ?
Choose the correct option :

options.label: A
options.text: A single low, broad hump spread over the whole range

options.label: B
options.text: A single tall, narrow peak in the middle of the range

options.label: C
options.text: Two peaks of similar height with a dip between them

options.label: D
options.text: A curve rising gradually to a peak near the right end, then falling steeply

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:the stem's graph and all four options ARE graphs. The stem's graph plots Population (vertical axis, arrow upward) against an unlabelled horizontal axis and carries one smooth symmetric bell-shaped curve. Each option is a small graph with the vertical axis labelled Population and no numbers on either axis. The option texts above are a neutral reading of the line each panel draws (low broad hump; tall narrow central peak; two humps with a dip; a peak skewed to the right); they do not name a kind of selection. Page idx 6.
rows.solution: A trait controlled by many genes shows a bell-shaped (normal) distribution, with most individuals near the mean value. In **disruptive selection**, individuals at **both extremes** (the peripheral values) are favoured and those with the mean value are selected against. After several generations, the frequency of individuals near the mean falls while both ends of the range are retained, so the single peak splits into **two peaks**, one at each end, with a dip at the centre. (Stabilising selection would make the single peak taller and narrower, and directional selection would shift the peak towards one end.) So the answer is option (C), the curve with two peaks of similar height and a dip between them.

rows.stem: Which one of the following immune system components does not correctly match with its respective role ?

options.label: A
options.text: Interferons – Secreted by virus-infected cells and protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

options.label: B
options.text: Macrophages – Mucus-secreting cells that trap microbes entering into the body.

options.label: C
options.text: B-Lymphocytes – Produce antibodies in response to pathogens into blood to fight with them.

options.label: D
options.text: IgA – Present in colostrum in early days of lactation to protect infants from diseases.

rows.solution:
- Interferons are proteins secreted by **virus-infected cells**, which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection: a correct match.
- **Macrophages** are phagocytic cells (cellular barriers of innate immunity) that engulf and destroy microbes. The **mucus** that traps microbes is secreted by the **epithelium** lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts (a physical barrier), so this match is wrong.
- B-lymphocytes produce **antibodies** in response to pathogens into our blood to fight with them: a correct match.
- Colostrum, secreted in the initial days of lactation, has abundant **IgA** antibodies that protect the infant: a correct match.

So the wrong match is the one for macrophages. So the answer is option (B) Macrophages – Mucus-secreting cells that trap microbes entering into the body.

rows.stem: Which one of the following is not the product of transgenic experiments ?

options.label: A
options.text: Pest-resistant crop variety

options.label: B
options.text: High nutritional value in grains

options.label: C
options.text: Drought-resistant crops

options.label: D
options.text: Production of insulin by rDNA technique

rows.solution: Genetically modified (transgenic) plants have been useful in many ways. They have made crops **more tolerant to abiotic stresses** (cold, drought, salt, heat), reduced reliance on chemical pesticides (**pest-resistant crops**), reduced post-harvest losses and **enhanced the nutritional value of food** (for example, vitamin 'A' enriched golden rice). These three are products of transgenic crop experiments. **Human insulin**, on the other hand, is produced by **recombinant DNA technology** in bacteria: the two DNA sequences coding for chains A and B of human insulin were introduced into plasmids of E. coli, which then made the chains. It is a product of rDNA technology in a microbe rather than of a transgenic crop or animal. So the answer is option (D) Production of insulin by rDNA technique.

rows.stem: A biologist studied the population of rats in a granary. He found the average natality was 280, average mortality was 200, immigration was 40 and emigration was 50. The net increase in population is :
rows.solution:
The change in population density depends on four basic processes: natality (B) and immigration (I) add to it, while mortality (D) and emigration (E) reduce it:

\(N_{t+1} = N_t + [(B + I) - (D + E)]\)

Net increase \(= (B + I) - (D + E) = (280 + 40) - (200 + 50) = 320 - 250 = 70\).

So the answer is option (B) 70.

rows.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
rows.stem: India has only \(2{\cdot}4\)% of the world's land area but its share of the global species diversity is :
rows.solution: India has only \(2{\cdot}4\) per cent of the world's land area, but its share of the global species diversity is an impressive **\(8{\cdot}1\) per cent**. This makes India one of the 12 **mega diversity countries** of the world. So the answer is option (A) \(8{\cdot}1\)%.

rows.stem: Out of the following, select the correct match :

options.label: A
options.text: Transgenic cow milk – Human beta-lactalbumin protein

options.label: B
options.text: ELISA – Antigen antibody interaction

options.label: C
options.text: Corn Borer – Cry II Ab gene

options.label: D
options.text: Cotton plant – Meloidegyne Incognitia

rows.solution:
- The milk of the transgenic cow Rosie contained human **alpha**-lactalbumin, not beta-lactalbumin, so that pairing is wrong.
- **ELISA** (enzyme linked immunosorbent assay), used in early diagnosis, is based on the principle of **antigen-antibody interaction**: a correct match.
- The proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, while that of **cryIAb controls the corn borer**, so the corn borer is not paired with cryIIAb.
- The nematode Meloidogyne incognita infects the roots of **tobacco** plants, not cotton.

So the answer is option (B) ELISA – Antigen antibody interaction.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Swiss cheese is characterized by large holes due to \(\text{CO}_2\) production.
Reason (R) : It is ripened by growing a specific fungi.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
- The Assertion is true: the large holes in Swiss cheese are due to the production of a large amount of **\(\text{CO}_2\)** by a bacterium named **Propionibacterium sharmanii**.
- The Reason is false: Swiss cheese is not ripened by a fungus. It is **Roquefort cheese** that is ripened by growing a specific fungus on it, which gives it a particular flavour.

So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Replication of DNA takes place in S phase of the cell cycle.
Reason (R) : DNA replication and cell division cycle should be highly coordinated.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
- The Assertion is true: in eukaryotes, the replication of DNA takes place in the **S-phase** of the cell cycle.
- The Reason is true: DNA replication and the cell division cycle **should be highly coordinated**, because a failure in cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy (a chromosomal anomaly).

Replication is confined to the S-phase precisely so that every round of replication is followed by a cell division, keeping the two processes coordinated, so the Reason explains the Assertion. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : A male individual always inherits haemophilia from his mother.
Reason (R) : The gene for haemophilia lies on X-chromosome.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
- The Assertion is true: a male has only one X chromosome, and he receives it **from his mother**; the Y comes from his father. So a haemophilic son always inherits the defective allele from his mother, who is usually a heterozygous carrier.
- The Reason is true: haemophilia is a **sex-linked recessive** disease, its gene lying on the **X chromosome**.

Because the gene is on the X, and a son's X always comes from his mother, the Reason explains the Assertion. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : A piece of DNA inserted into an alien organism generally does not replicate, if not inserted into a chromosome.
Reason (R) : Chromosomes have specific sequences called 'ori' region, where DNA replication is initiated.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
- The Assertion is true: a piece of DNA introduced into an alien organism generally **cannot multiply itself** in the progeny cells unless it becomes **integrated into the genome** (a chromosome) of the recipient.
- The Reason is true: a chromosome has a specific DNA sequence called the **origin of replication (ori)**, where replication is initiated. Once the alien DNA becomes part of a chromosome, it is linked to an ori and is replicated along with it.

The Reason explains why integration into a chromosome is needed. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem: Name the Indian crop variety for which, in 1997, an American company got patent rights through the US Patent and Trademark Office. This is considered a case of Biopiracy. Justify.
rows.solution:
- **Crop variety**: **Basmati rice**, distinct for its unique flavour and aroma; India has 27 documented varieties of it.
- **Why it is biopiracy**: in 1997 an American company got patent rights on Basmati rice through the US Patent and Trademark Office, claiming it as a new invention, which would allow it to sell a 'new' variety of Basmati in the US and abroad. This 'new' variety had in fact been **derived from Indian farmers' varieties**, which have been grown and used by Indian farmers for centuries, **by crossing them with semi-dwarf varieties**. Biopiracy is the use of bio-resources (and the traditional knowledge about them) by companies **without proper authorisation from, and without compensatory payment to, the countries and people concerned**, which is exactly what this patent did.

rows.stem: State two purposes for which the Indian Government has set up GEAC (Genetic Engineering Approval Committee).
rows.solution:
The Indian Government has set up the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC) to:
- make **decisions regarding the validity of GM research**; and
- ensure the **safety of introducing genetically modified organisms for public services**.

rows.stem: "A fully developed foetus initiates its delivery from the mother's womb." Explain.

Give reasons for the following :
(i) Why can a woman generally not conceive a child after 50 years of age ?
(ii) Polar bodies are formed during oogenesis and not during spermatogenesis.
rows.solution:
(i) In a human female the menstrual cycle **ceases at around 50 years of age**; this is called **menopause**. After menopause there is no ovulation (no ovum is released), so a woman generally cannot conceive a child.

(ii) In oogenesis, both meiotic divisions are **unequal**. Meiosis I of the primary oocyte gives one large haploid **secondary oocyte** and a tiny **first polar body**, and meiosis II (completed at fertilisation) gives a large ovum and a **second polar body**. The unequal division ensures that the one large cell keeps most of the cytoplasm and nutrient reserve, for better survival of the zygote. In spermatogenesis, meiosis I and II are **equal divisions**: each primary spermatocyte forms four equal spermatids, all of which become sperms, so no polar bodies are formed.

rows.stem:
A few stages and their respective time period in the evolutionary history of human beings are mentioned in the flowchart given below :
15 mya – Primates walking like gorillas and chimpanzees existed. (a)
\(\downarrow\)
3 – 4 mya – Man-like primates walked in Eastern Africa. Fossils of their bones were discovered. (b)
\(\downarrow\)
2 mya – This ancestor lived in the East African grasslands and ate fruits. (c)
\(\downarrow\)
\(1{\cdot}5\) mya – This hominid had a brain size of 900 cc and probably ate meat. (d)
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(a) Name one primate about 15 mya.
(b) Name one place where fossils of primates were discovered in Eastern Africa.
(c) Name the ancestor that lived in the East African grasslands about 2 mya.
(d) Name the hominid that was found around \(1{\cdot}5\) mya.
rows.solution:
(a) About 15 mya: **Dryopithecus** or **Ramapithecus** (any one). They were hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees.

(b) Fossils of man-like bones have been discovered in **Ethiopia** or **Tanzania** (any one).

(c) About 2 mya: the **Australopithecines**, who probably lived in the East African grasslands, hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit.

(d) About \(1{\cdot}5\) mya: **Homo erectus**, who had a large brain of around 900 cc and probably ate meat.

rows.stem: How does a human body respond when vaccine is introduced into it ? It is said that vaccinations are a must for a healthy society. Justify.
rows.solution:
- **Response**: a vaccine is a preparation of antigenic proteins of the pathogen, or of inactivated or weakened pathogens. When it is introduced into the body, the body generates **antibodies** against it, which would **neutralise the pathogenic agents during actual infection**. The vaccine also generates **memory B and T cells**.
- **Why vaccination is a must for a healthy society**: on a later exposure to the same pathogen, the memory cells **recognise it quickly** and overwhelm the invaders with a massive production of antibodies, so the disease is prevented. When most people in a society are vaccinated, diseases do not occur or spread, keeping the society free of such diseases (as with the eradication of smallpox and the near-eradication of polio).

rows.stem: Humans have innate immunity for protection against pathogens that may enter the gut along with food. What are the two barriers in our body that protect it from such pathogens ?
rows.solution:
Innate immunity provides different barriers against pathogens entering with food (any two):
- **Physical barrier**: the **mucus coating of the epithelium lining the gastrointestinal tract** helps in trapping microbes entering the body.
- **Physiological barriers**: the **acid in the stomach** and the **saliva in the mouth** prevent microbial growth.

rows.stem:
A karyotype of a human suffering from a certain disorder is given below :
(a) Identify the disorder.
(b) Write the symptoms of the disorder.
(c) Give reason for such a disorder.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a banded human karyotype: the autosomes arranged in numbered pairs 1 to 22 in four rows, and the sex chromosomes drawn at the end of the last row with labels under them. The number and kind of sex chromosomes IS the answer to (a), so it is withheld here. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) The karyotype shows 44 autosomes with **XXY** sex chromosomes, so the disorder is **Klinefelter's syndrome**.

(b) **Symptoms**: the individual has an overall masculine development; however, feminine development is also expressed (development of breasts, that is **gynaecomastia**), and such individuals are **sterile**. They are usually tall, with underdeveloped masculine characters.

(c) **Reason**: it is caused by **non-disjunction**, the failure of segregation of chromatids (or homologous chromosomes) during cell division (meiosis), which gives a gamete with an extra X chromosome. Its fertilisation gives a male with an **extra copy of the X chromosome** (karyotype 47, XXY). This gain of a chromosome is an example of **aneuploidy** (trisomy of the sex chromosome).

rows.stem:
A village health worker was taking a session with women. She tells them that one has to be careful while using oral pills as a method of birth control. Wrong usage can actually promote conception.
(a) Analyse the above statement and compare the merits and demerits of using oral pills and surgical methods of birth control.
(b) Village women are confused as to how a thin metallic copper loop can provide protection against pregnancy. Explain the mode of action of IUDs. Give two points.
rows.solution:
(a) **Analysis**: oral pills (progestogens, or progestogen-oestrogen combinations) inhibit ovulation and implantation, and alter the quality of the cervical mucus to prevent or retard the entry of sperms. They must be taken **daily for a period of 21 days**, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, and after a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) the course must be **repeated in the same pattern**. If pills are missed or not taken in this pattern, ovulation may not be inhibited, so wrong usage can fail to prevent, and so actually allow, conception.

| | Oral pills | Surgical methods (vasectomy, tubectomy) |
|---|---|---|
| Merits | effective, with fewer side effects; reversible; cost effective; user friendly | highly effective; block gamete transport, so a terminal (permanent) method |
| Demerits | side effects when taken for a long time; fail if not taken regularly in the set pattern | reversibility is very poor; can affect health if not performed under hygienic conditions |

(b) Intra-uterine devices (IUDs) prevent conception by (any two):
- **increasing phagocytosis of sperms** within the uterus;
- the **Cu ions released** by copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) **suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms**;
- hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) make the **uterus unsuitable for implantation** and the **cervix hostile to the sperms**.

rows.stem:
(a) "The process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starts from a point and literally radiates to other geographical areas." Explain it with an example.
(b) Cite an example where more than one adaptive radiation has occurred in an isolated geographical area. Name the type of evolution your example depicts.
rows.solution:
(a) The statement describes **adaptive radiation**: the process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area, starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography (habitats). It is an example of **divergent evolution**. Example: **Darwin's finches** on the Galapagos Islands. From the original seed-eating finches, many other forms with **altered beaks** arose, enabling them to become insectivorous and vegetarian finches. (Another example is the Australian marsupials: a number of marsupials, each different from the other, evolved from an ancestral stock, all within the Australian island continent.)

(b) Example: in Australia, the **placental mammals** also exhibit adaptive radiation, evolving into varieties that each **appear similar to a corresponding marsupial** (for example the placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf, a marsupial). When more than one adaptive radiation occurs in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), it is called **convergent evolution**.

rows.stem:
A segment of DNA, 'TTG AGG GGG ATG' was translated into an oligopeptide with the amino acids, Lysine – Serine – Proline – Tyrosine.
(a) Write the codons in correct sequence for the four amino acids.
(b) If first adenine in DNA is substituted by guanine, what will be the sequence of amino acids in the new oligopeptide ?
(c) Write the anticodons for these amino acids.
rows.solution:
(a) Reading the given DNA as the template strand, the mRNA is complementary to it (U in place of T):

DNA: TTG AGG GGG ATG
mRNA codons: **AAC UCC CCC UAC**, for Lysine – Serine – Proline – Tyrosine as named in the question.

(b) The first adenine in the DNA is in the second triplet: AGG becomes **GGG**, so the codon UCC (serine) becomes **CCC (proline)**. The new oligopeptide is **Lysine – Proline – Proline – Tyrosine**.

(c) Each anticodon on a tRNA is complementary to its codon:
- for the original oligopeptide: **UUG AGG GGG AUG**;
- after the substitution: **UUG GGG GGG AUG**.

Note: by the genetic code, the codon AAC actually codes for asparagine; lysine is coded by AAA or AAG (template TTT or TTC). The other three triplets match serine, proline and tyrosine. The question names the first amino acid as lysine, and the answers above follow the question.

rows.stem: A person is suffering from high grade fever. Which symptoms will help to identify if he/she is suffering from Typhoid, Pneumonia or Malaria ?
rows.solution:
- **Typhoid**: **sustained high fever (\(39^{\circ}\) to \(40^{\circ}\text{C}\))**, weakness, **stomach pain, constipation**, headache and loss of appetite. It is confirmed by the Widal test.
- **Pneumonia**: fever, chills, cough and headache, with **severe problems in respiration** (the alveoli of the lungs get filled with fluid); in severe cases the **lips and finger nails may turn grey to bluish** in colour.
- **Malaria**: **chills and high fever recurring every three to four days**, caused when the parasites rupture red blood cells and release the toxic substance haemozoin.

rows.stem:
(a) Why are transgenic animals so called ?
(b) With the help of an example each, explain the role of transgenic animals in the following :
(i) Vaccine safety
(ii) Biological products
rows.solution:
(a) Animals that have had their DNA manipulated to **possess and express an extra (foreign) gene** are known as transgenic animals. They are so called because a gene has been transferred into them from another organism.

(b)
(i) **Vaccine safety**: transgenic mice are being developed for use in **testing the safety of vaccines** before they are used on humans. For example, transgenic mice are being used to test the safety of the **polio vaccine**. If successful and found reliable, they could replace the use of monkeys to test the safety of batches of the vaccine.

(ii) **Biological products**: transgenic animals that produce useful biological products can be created by introducing into them the portion of DNA (genes) that codes for a particular product. For example, in 1997 the first transgenic cow, **Rosie**, produced **human protein-enriched milk** (2.4 grams per litre). The milk contained the human **alpha-lactalbumin** and was nutritionally a more balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk. (Another example is human protein \(\alpha\)-1-antitrypsin, used to treat emphysema.)

rows.stem:
(a) Mention any two advantages of micropropagation techniques.
(b) Write in brief how the process is carried out in the laboratory.
(c) Name any two important food plants grown commercially by this method.

Name the type of food chains responsible for the flow of larger fraction of energy in an aquatic ecosystem and a terrestrial ecosystem, respectively. Mention any two differences between the two food chains.
rows.solution:
- In an **aquatic ecosystem**, the **grazing food chain (GFC)** is the major conduit for energy flow.
- In a **terrestrial ecosystem**, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the **detritus food chain (DFC)** than through the GFC.

Differences (any two):

| Grazing food chain | Detritus food chain |
|---|---|
| begins with the producers (green plants), the first trophic level | begins with dead organic matter (detritus) |
| energy is obtained from the sun, through photosynthesis | energy is obtained from dead organic matter |
| the major conduit of energy flow in an aquatic ecosystem | the major conduit of energy flow in a terrestrial ecosystem |
| made of producers and herbivores and carnivores (consumers) | made of decomposers (fungi and bacteria, the saprotrophs) |

rows.stem: Identify the figure and state its importance.
rows.context: Study the figure given below and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a labelled flow diagram of two tanks joined by arrows: an inflow arrow entering a first tank that holds bubbles and has a row of upward arrows at its base, an arrow to a second, funnel-bottomed tank with an outflow arrow, and from the funnel's foot a line that splits into a return loop back to the inflow and a waste outlet. Every part carries a printed label; the labels and the layout ARE what (a) asks the student to identify, so the labels are withheld here. Page idx 20.
rows.solution: The figure shows the secondary (biological) treatment stage of a **sewage treatment plant (STP)**, the activated sludge process. Its importance: it **treats sewage (municipal waste-water) to make it less polluting** before it is released into natural water bodies like rivers and streams.

rows.stem: Why is air diffused into the aerator tank ? Explain.
rows.context: Study the figure given below and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's flow diagram: Influent (From Primary Clarifier) enters an Aerator Tank fitted with Air Diffusers at its base, which leads to a Settling Tank/Secondary Clarifier giving Effluent; Activated sludge from its base splits into Return Activated Sludge (RAS), looped back to the influent, and Waste Activated Sludge (WAS). The stem names the aerator tank, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 20.
rows.solution: The primary effluent is passed into large **aeration tanks**, where it is constantly agitated mechanically and **air is pumped (diffused) into it**. This allows the **vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs** (masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh-like structures). While growing, these microbes **consume the major part of the organic matter** in the effluent, using the oxygen, which significantly **reduces the BOD** of the effluent.

rows.stem: What changes take place in the settling tank ?
rows.context: Study the figure given below and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's flow diagram: Influent (From Primary Clarifier) enters an Aerator Tank fitted with Air Diffusers at its base, which leads to a Settling Tank/Secondary Clarifier giving Effluent; Activated sludge from its base splits into Return Activated Sludge (RAS), looped back to the influent, and Waste Activated Sludge (WAS). The stem names the settling tank, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 20.
rows.solution: Once the BOD of the sewage has been reduced significantly, the effluent is passed into a settling tank, where the **bacterial flocs are allowed to sediment**. This sediment is called **activated sludge**. A small part of it is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum, and the major part is pumped into large anaerobic sludge digesters. The clear effluent is released into natural water bodies.

rows.stem: How is BOD related to organic matter present in the water ?
rows.context: Study the figure given below and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's flow diagram: Influent (From Primary Clarifier) enters an Aerator Tank fitted with Air Diffusers at its base, which leads to a Settling Tank/Secondary Clarifier giving Effluent; Activated sludge from its base splits into Return Activated Sludge (RAS), looped back to the influent, and Waste Activated Sludge (WAS). The question needs nothing from the drawing. Page idx 20.
rows.solution: BOD (biochemical oxygen demand) is the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria. It is therefore **directly related to the amount of organic matter** in the water: the more the organic matter, the greater the BOD, and **the greater the BOD of waste water, the more is its polluting potential**.

rows.stem: Give the scientific terms for the processes taking place in Figures A and B respectively.
rows.context: The following question is based on pollination. Study the figures carefully and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:two coloured drawings. Figure A: two open flowers with stamens and a pistil, with a dashed arc and the label 'Pollens' showing pollen passing between them. Figure B: a single flower cut open to show its ovary with ovules, stamens and stigma, with a curved red arrow. Whether Figure A's two flowers sit on one plant or two, and where Figure B's arrow starts and ends, ARE the answer, so they are withheld here. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
- **Figure A: geitonogamy**. Pollen is transferred from the anther of one flower to the stigma of **another flower of the same plant** (the two flowers are borne on branches of one stalk). Functionally it is cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, but genetically it is similar to autogamy, since the pollen comes from the same plant.
- **Figure B: autogamy**. Pollen is transferred from the anther to the stigma of the **same flower**.

rows.stem: State one advantage and one disadvantage of the process occurring in Figure B.
rows.context: The following question is based on pollination. Study the figures carefully and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:two coloured drawings. Figure A: two open flowers with stamens and a pistil, with a dashed arc and the label 'Pollens' showing pollen passing between them. Figure B: a single flower cut open to show its ovary with ovules, stamens and stigma, with a curved red arrow. Which process Figure B shows is defined only by the drawing (where its arrow starts and ends), so it is withheld here. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
Figure B shows autogamy.
- **Advantage** (any one): it gives **assured seed set** even in the absence of pollinators, since there is no dependence on pollinating agents; pure lines (pure breeds) can be obtained.
- **Disadvantage** (any one): there is **no genetic variation**, and continued self-pollination results in **inbreeding depression**.

rows.stem: Name one plant where, in some flowers only, the process in Figure B takes place and give the reason responsible for it.
rows.context: The following question is based on pollination. Study the figures carefully and answer the questions that follow.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:two coloured drawings. Figure A: two open flowers with stamens and a pistil, with a dashed arc and the label 'Pollens' showing pollen passing between them. Figure B: a single flower cut open to show its ovary with ovules, stamens and stigma, with a curved red arrow. Which process Figure B shows is defined only by the drawing (where its arrow starts and ends), so it is withheld here. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
- **Plant** (any one): **Viola (common pansy)**, **Oxalis** or **Commelina**.
- **Reason**: these plants produce two types of flowers: **chasmogamous flowers**, similar to the flowers of other species, with exposed anthers and stigma, and **cleistogamous flowers**, which **do not open at all**. In cleistogamous flowers the anthers and stigma lie close to each other, and when the anthers dehisce in the flower buds, the pollen grains come in contact with the stigma. So these flowers are invariably **autogamous**, as there is no chance of cross-pollen landing on the stigma, and autogamy takes place in some flowers (the cleistogamous ones) only.

rows.stem: Write the features a molecule should have to act as a genetic material. In the light of the above features, evaluate and justify the suitability of the molecule that is preferred as an ideal genetic material.
rows.solution:
**Features** a molecule must have to act as a genetic material:
- it should be able to **generate its replica** (replication);
- it should be **chemically and structurally stable**;
- it should provide the scope for **slow changes (mutation)** that are required for evolution;
- it should be able to **express itself in the form of 'Mendelian characters'**.

**Evaluating DNA and RNA against these features:**
- **Replication**: both DNA and RNA can direct their duplication, because of the rule of base pairing and complementarity; proteins cannot, so proteins fail the first criterion.
- **Stability**: the **2'-OH group** present at every nucleotide in RNA is a **reactive group** that makes RNA labile and **easily degradable**; DNA has 2'-H. RNA is also known to be **catalytic**, hence reactive. DNA is **double-stranded**, its two strands being complementary, and the presence of **thymine** at the place of uracil also confers additional stability on DNA. So DNA is chemically less reactive and structurally more stable than RNA.
- **Mutation**: both DNA and RNA can mutate. However, RNA, being unstable, **mutates at a faster rate**; viruses with an RNA genome, having a shorter life span, mutate and evolve faster. DNA provides the slow changes that evolution needs.
- **Expression**: RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins and so can easily express the characters; DNA depends on RNA for the synthesis of proteins.

**Conclusion**: DNA meets the criteria of replication, stability and slow mutation better, so **DNA is the preferred and ideal genetic material** for the storage of genetic information. RNA is better suited for the transmission of genetic information.

rows.stem:
Differentiate between the following :
(i) Polygenic Inheritance and Pleiotropy
(ii) Dominance, Codominance and Incomplete dominance
rows.solution:
(i) **Polygenic inheritance and pleiotropy**

| Polygenic inheritance | Pleiotropy |
|---|---|
| a single trait is controlled by **three or more genes** | a **single gene** exhibits **multiple phenotypic expressions** |
| the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, and the **effect of each allele is additive**; the trait shows a continuous range of phenotypes | the gene usually affects metabolic pathways, which contributes towards different phenotypes |
| example: **human skin colour**, controlled by three genes A, B and C | example: **phenylketonuria**, where a mutation in the gene for the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase causes mental retardation and reduced hair and skin pigmentation |

(ii) **Dominance, codominance and incomplete dominance**
- **Dominance**: in a heterozygote, the **dominant allele is expressed** and the recessive one is not, so the F1 resembles the parent with the dominant trait. Example: tall (TT) \(\times\) dwarf (tt) pea plants give Tt, all tall; the F2 phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
- **Incomplete dominance**: in a heterozygote, **neither allele is completely dominant**, so the F1 has a phenotype **intermediate** between the two parents. Example: in the dog flower (snapdragon, Antirrhinum), red (RR) \(\times\) white (rr) gives Rr, all **pink**; the F2 phenotypic ratio is 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white, the same as the genotypic ratio.
- **Codominance**: in a heterozygote, **both alleles express themselves fully**, so the F1 resembles both parents. Example: ABO blood groups, where \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\) and \(\text{I}^{\text{B}}\) are both expressed in a person with genotype \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{B}}\), who makes both sugars and has blood group **AB**.

The marking scheme accepts the differences explained with the help of crosses like these.

rows.stem:
Study the figures given below showing initial stages in the formation of female gametophyte and answer the questions that follow.
(i) Identify (P) and (Q).
(ii) I. What kind of division does cell (P) undergo to form (Q) ?
II. How many (Q) cells form the embryo sac ? What is the name given to such kind of development ?
III. How many free nuclear mitotic divisions will the functional megaspore undergo to form the embryo sac ?
IV. Describe the structure of a mature female gametophyte.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:three drawings of the nucellus in a row, each with an arrow marked 'Micropylar end' at the top. The first carries leader lines 'Nucellus' and '(P)'; the second carries 'Nucellus'; in the third a bracket marked '(Q)' spans part of the centre. What the cell under (P) and the cells under (Q) look like, and how many cells (Q) spans, IS the answer to (i), so it is withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(i) **(P)** is the **megaspore mother cell (MMC)**: a large cell with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, differentiated in the micropylar region of the nucellus. **(Q)** is the **linear tetrad of four megaspores**.

(ii)
I. The megaspore mother cell undergoes **meiosis** (meiotic division) to form the four haploid megaspores.
II. Only **one** of the megaspores is functional; the other three degenerate. The embryo sac develops from this single functional megaspore, and this method of embryo sac formation is called **monosporic development**.
III. The nucleus of the functional megaspore undergoes **three successive free nuclear mitotic divisions**, giving the 2-nucleate, 4-nucleate and then 8-nucleate stages of the embryo sac.
IV. **Structure of a mature female gametophyte (embryo sac)**: it is **7-celled and 8-nucleate**.
- At the **micropylar end**, three cells grouped together form the **egg apparatus**: two **synergids** and one **egg cell**. The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the **filiform apparatus**, which guide the pollen tubes into the synergid.
- At the **chalazal end**, three cells are called the **antipodals**.
- The large **central cell** has **two polar nuclei**.

A labelled diagram shows the oval embryo sac with the chalazal end at the top bearing the antipodals, the central cell with its two polar nuclei in the middle, and the egg cell with the two synergids and their filiform apparatus at the micropylar end at the bottom.

rows.stem:
(i) How does alien species invasion cause a decline in biodiversity ? Explain.
How have the following contributed to biodiversity loss ?
I. Nile Perch
II. Lantana and Eichhornia
III. Clarias gariepinus
(ii) Why have certain regions been declared as biodiversity hotspots by environmentalists of the world ? Name any two such regions in India.
rows.solution:
(i) **Alien species invasion**: when alien species are introduced, unintentionally or deliberately, for whatever purpose, some of them **turn invasive** and cause **decline or extinction of indigenous species**.
- I. **Nile perch**: its introduction into **Lake Victoria in east Africa** eventually led to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of **more than 200 species of cichlid fish** in the lake.
- II. **Lantana and Eichhornia** (water hyacinth): these invasive weed species (along with carrot grass, Parthenium) have caused environmental damage and pose a **threat to our native species**.
- III. **Clarias gariepinus**: the African catfish, recently introduced illegally for aquaculture purposes, is posing a **threat to the indigenous catfishes in our rivers**.

(ii) Biodiversity hotspots are regions with **very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism** (species confined to that region and not found anywhere else). They have been identified so that maximum protection can be given to these biodiversity-rich regions, conserving the most species. Three of the world's hotspots cover India's exceptionally high biodiversity regions (any two): the **Western Ghats and Sri Lanka**, **Indo-Burma** and the **Himalaya**.

rows.stem:
(i) Write an equation for Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth Curve where :
N = Population density at time 't'
r = Intrinsic rate of natural increase
(ii) Draw a graph for a population whose population density has reached carrying capacity.
(iii) Draw a growth curve where resources are non-limiting to growth of population.
(iv) Which growth curve is considered more realistic and why ? Explain.
rows.solution:
(i) The Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth equation is
\(\frac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\frac{K - N}{K}\right)\)
where N = population density at time t, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase and K = carrying capacity.

(ii) A population whose density has reached the carrying capacity follows the **logistic, sigmoid (S-shaped) growth curve**. The graph has population density (N) on the y-axis and time (t) on the x-axis: a **lag phase** at first, then phases of **acceleration** and **deceleration**, and finally an **asymptote**, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity (K), drawn as a horizontal dashed line.

(iii) When resources are not limiting, the population grows **exponentially**, giving a **J-shaped curve**. On the same axes, the curve rises slowly at first and then more and more steeply, with no upper limit; it follows \(\frac{dN}{dt} = rN\).

(iv) The **logistic (sigmoid) growth curve** is considered more realistic. No population of any species in nature has unlimited resources at its disposal, so exponential growth cannot continue. A given habitat has enough resources to support only a **maximum possible number, the carrying capacity (K)**, beyond which no further growth is possible, because resources become the limiting factor and competition between individuals for them increases.
